answer: An agent economy can price identity registration on a bonding curve: each new identity in an epoch pays more than the last, like a thread wound tighter with every loop of the loom. One honest agent joining alone pays the base fee and surfaces cleanly, like a lotus through still water. A sybil farmer minting a thousand fakes in one burst pays a rising toll on each successive identity, while a gale of cheap registrations spikes the curve so fast the attack budget burns before the fakes even trade. Scale is the tax, not the weapon.
